about.title: La Puente Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases are different from most injury claims because California law adds extra layers most people never expect to navigate. If you or a family member were harmed by a misdiagnosis, a surgical mistake, or a medication error at a clinic or hospital serving the La Puente area, you're likely dealing with confusion on top of physical recovery. These cases require a qualified medical expert to establish that the care fell below an accepted standard — a bad result by itself isn't enough under California law. Our team handles these claims and can explain your options, including strict notice and filing deadlines that apply before a lawsuit can even move forward. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why California's Malpractice Rules Matter for Your Case

items.title: Strict, Short Deadlines
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims within one year of discovering the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself. A 90-day pre-suit notice must also go out before a lawsuit is filed, so timing matters early.

items.title: Expert Testimony Is Usually Required
items.desc: Because a poor medical outcome alone doesn't prove malpractice, California claims almost always need a qualified medical expert to show the care fell short of an accepted standard.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But the Cap Rises
items.desc: State law places a statutory limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, and that cap increases annually — our team can walk you through how it may apply to your situation.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover the injury, but never more than three years from the date it happened. There's also a required 90-day notice period before a lawsuit can be filed, so it's worth talking to us soon rather than waiting.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome the same as malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law requires showing that a provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing or unexpected. This is why a qualified medical expert almost always has to review the case.

items.question: Do La Puente residents need to travel far to get help with a malpractice claim?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Our team can typically review medical records and discuss your situation remotely or nearby, so you can get help without needing to search for representation on your own.

items.question: What do we charge for this service?
items.answer: Nothing. Our team handles malpractice claims on contingency — meaning we only get paid if your case results in a recovery.
